_comment: Vendor manifest (example). Copy, edit, and point VENDOR_MANIFEST at it.
Declares files you keep as RESIDENT COPIES on purpose, rather than as shims over the upstream
engine. Most consumer scripts should be shims, so an upstream fix arrives with no manual step.
Some cannot be: a file called by a gate in another repository, on machines where this project
was never cloned, must not exit when the engine is absent.
Those copies then get documented as 'kept in sync by hand', which is a hope rather than a
control. One drifted to 311 lines against upstream's 416, missing an entire flag and four
functions, and nothing noticed, because a stale analyzer reports cheerfully.
vendor-audit reports that UPSTREAM MOVED since reconciliation. It never reports that the two
files differ: they always differ, that is the point of the copy, and a check that fires
It also does not auto-sync in either direction, deliberately. Pulling upstream over a resident
copy discards local configuration; pushing the other way leaks consumer specifics into a
portable core. The machine notices, a human reconciles, --adopt records the new baseline.

entries.why_resident: called by the memory backup repo's pre-commit gate, which lives in a different repository and must work on machines with no clone of the engine here
_comment: why_resident is REQUIRED. A vendored copy with no stated reason cannot be told apart from an
accident, which is how the drifted one got lost.
Relative paths resolve against this manifest's own directory, so it stays portable between
checkouts. Upstream being ABSENT is not drift: a machine without the source checked out is
the exact situation a resident copy exists for.

_comment_recipe: The vendoring shape that makes re-syncing cheap: a consumer preamble, a marker line, then the
upstream file byte for byte. Re-vendoring is then a concatenation, and the diff to review is
